records.text: Candace Owens said churches were intentionally closed, destroyed, or burned under communist rule and that state atheism was mandated.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Their church is intentionally closed, destroyed, burned, state atheism mandated.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The Soviet state promoted official atheism, confiscated religious property, closed or destroyed churches, and persecuted clergy and believers, although intensity varied over time.

sources.title: Internal Workings of the Soviet Union – Library of Congress
sources.relevance: Documents state atheism and the Soviet campaign against religious institutions.

records.text: Candace Owens cited a New York Times article saying the Soviet government financed its New York bureau by smuggling diamonds into New York by 1918.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: By 1918, the Soviet Union was financing the Soviet Bureau by smuggling diamonds into New York.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The New York Times profile describes Soviet financing of the New York bureau and the transfer/sale of diamonds and other valuables through the Hammer network during the early Soviet period.

sources.title: The Riddle of Armand Hammer – The New York Times Magazine
sources.relevance: Direct source for Soviet financing and diamond/valuable transfers through the New York operation.

records.text: Nikita Khrushchev said that a powerful fleet based at Sazan Island could put the Mediterranean from the Bosporus to Gibraltar under Soviet control.
records.speaker: Nikita Khrushchev

appearances.snippet: And according to Enver Hoxha, who was the former prime minister of Albania and was present, Khrushchev said of the island, quote, with a powerful fleet from here, we can have the whole of the Mediterranean, the Bosporus to Gibraltar, in our hands. We can control everyone, end quote.

verification.notes: Enver Hoxhas memoir records Khrushchev and Marshal Malinovsky saying from the Vlora-area villa at Uji i Ftohte that a powerful fleet could place the Mediterranean from the Bosporus to Gibraltar in their hands. The quotation is supported, but the source locates it at the Vlora bay area rather than specifically on or at Sazan Island, so the extracted location is overstated.

sources.title: The Khrushchevites, chapter 12
sources.relevance: Primary memoir source contains the quoted words and places them at Uji i Ftohte near Vlora.
